negative_findings.description: Targeted searching of Finextra for Hungarian banking/payments appointments returned only non-Hungarian items (Brite, Standard Chartered, FCA, Versapay, Stax). No Hungary-specific personnel article surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Finextra is a valid channel by structure but has near-zero observed Hungary personnel yield; keep it as a keyword tripwire, not a primary feed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents over-weighting a globally prominent trade outlet that in practice does not cover the Hungarian market's personnel layer.

negative_findings.description: Searches aimed at The Paypers for Hungarian payments appointments returned nothing from thepaypers.com; results drifted to UK 'Payments Association' CEO news and PayPal. The Paypers' Hungary personnel coverage could not be evidenced in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: No thepaypers.com Hungary appointment item found; the outlet remains a plausible but unevidenced channel.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A seed query assumption did not hold; the cell's payments-press coverage rests mainly on scheme newsrooms and FinTech Futures instead.

negative_findings.description: No PaymentsSource/American Banker item on Hungarian personnel was surfaced, and no dedicated Emerging Europe (emerging-europe.com) article on Hungarian banking appointments appeared despite a targeted query.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two named seed outlets produced zero Hungary personnel evidence in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These should be revisited with entity-specific queries (OTP, MBH, K&H, Erste Hungary, Raiffeisen Hungary) before being written off.

negative_findings.description: A Hungarian-language control query ('kinevezés vezérigazgató bank ... sajtóközlemény Erste Raiffeisen UniCredit') returned rich HU-only coverage (Portfolio.hu on the new Raiffeisen CEO and accompanying personnel changes, azenpenzem.hu, n4b.hu press-release wire, Erste Bank HU sajtóközlemények, Magyar Bankszövetség governing bodies page) with no matching English releases from the same groups.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian-owned/HU-subsidiary appointment news is systematically published in HU first and often only in HU; the English layer covers it partially and later.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms this English cell cannot stand alone — it must be paired with the hu-press cell, and English-only monitoring will miss or delay a large share of Hungarian bank personnel events.

negative_findings.description: The two highest-credibility international wires in this cell (Bloomberg, Reuters) are paywalled and bot-defended; their Hungary personnel items were only visible as headlines or via syndication mirrors (MarketScreener, Investing.com).
negative_findings.result_summary: Wire content is reachable in principle but not freely collectible; treat as unverified-but-live and route via licensed access or mirrors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must budget for licensing or accept mirror-based, delayed and partial capture of the fastest-breaking items.

coverage_gaps.description: No English-language newsroom was located in this pass for the Hungarian subsidiaries of Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, K&H/KBC and MBH Bank — only group-level or HU-language pages surfaced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Directly enumerate and crawl the /en/ press sections of erstebank.hu, raiffeisen.hu, unicreditbank.hu, kh.hu, mbhbank.hu, plus group IR newsrooms (erstegroup.com, rbinternational.com, unicreditgroup.eu, kbc.com), and record which actually mirror Hungary appointments into English.

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage found is almost entirely about senior appointments; the 'jobs/hiring' topic (headcount, recruitment drives, layoffs, shared-service-centre staffing in Budapest) is unrepresented in this English cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add English job-board and employer-brand sources for Hungary (LinkedIn company pages of OTP/MBH/Citi/Morgan Stanley Budapest, Budapest shared-service-centre coverage in BBJ's tech/HR sections) in a follow-up pass.

coverage_gaps.description: The payments half of the sector is thinly covered in English at the Hungary level: apart from Mastercard/Visa scheme newsrooms, no English source was found covering Hungarian PSPs, acquirers or fintechs (e.g. Barion, OTP Mobil/Simple, Nexi/SIA Hungary, Diebold/Printec-type vendors).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run entity-named English queries for Hungarian PSP/fintech leadership and check Nexi, Worldline, Global Payments and Euronet group newsrooms for Hungary/CEE country-lead announcements.

coverage_gaps.description: No structured/machine-readable disclosure channel was captured for this cell beyond issuer pages: the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE/BÉT) English regulatory-announcement feed, where OTP and other listed financials file appointment disclosures, was not reached.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and register the BÉT/BSE English 'company news' disclosure feed and the MNB market-supervision publication register as primary, timestamped sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Several strong candidates (BBJ appointments section, FinTech Futures job-cuts vertical) were identified structurally, but the depth and stability of their archives — pagination limits, URL scheme changes such as BBJ's /whosnews/ to /business/people/appointments/ migration — were not tested.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run an archive-depth probe per source and record earliest reachable item plus URL-scheme history before designing the historical backfill.

brief: English-language coverage of Hungarian banking and payments personnel is anchored by one genuinely strong source — the Budapest Business Journal's appointments column (plus its legacy 'Who's News' archive) — supported by issuer and scheme newsrooms (OTP Group's English IR site, Citi Hungary, Mastercard Europe, Visa CEMEA) and the MNB's English pressroom as the authoritative confirmation layer. The international wires (Bloomberg, Reuters) break the biggest moves first but are paywalled and bot-defended, so in practice they are reachable only through licensing or syndication mirrors such as MarketScreener and Investing.com; bne IntelliNews adds CEE strategic context behind a subscription. Global payments trade press (Finextra, The Paypers, FinTech Futures, PaymentsSource) proved structurally right but empirically almost empty of Hungary-specific personnel items, so it should be run as a keyword tripwire rather than a primary feed. A Hungarian-language control query confirmed a systematic language asymmetry — Portfolio.hu and the HU press carry Raiffeisen/Erste/UniCredit Hungary appointments that never appear in English — so this cell must be treated as a partial, lagging mirror of the hu-press cell, not a substitute.
